threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'pavement', not a 'sidewalk'. Local kids just call it the play area behind the shops, like it’s an unspoken rule.
Last night on the 77, a guy tried to impress a girl by claiming he invented the kebab. She was more interested in the cold chips spilled on the floor.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy juggling flaming torches at the Tempelhofer Feld while a group of kids flew kites nearby. Pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that opens at 3 AM, serving fresh dürüm to the club crowd. It’s the perfect late-night ritual.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know to avoid the BART on Fridays—brakes overheat and half the trains are delayed. Weekend vibes in chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, saw a guy juggling while waiting for the 21. He caught a bus token mid-air right as the bus pulled up. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think pa amb tomàquet is just a snack, but locals see it as a sacred ritual. Missing the right bread? You might as well skip it altogether.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their fresh excitement for the plaça's hidden corners, while locals casually ignore the same spots.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still get confused at the bus stop when the driver doesn’t bother to announce the stops. Proper locals just know when to jump off.
Caught a guy on the 57 chatting up the driver about how he once found a lost pet hamster on a bus. Driver seemed genuinely interested.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids using old subway tickets as skateboards on the sidewalk—only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find a techno party in a public sauna here. Only in Berlin do you sweat it out in drum and bass during the day and dance at night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know the exact bus schedule for the 22 Fillmore, even with the delays. Tourists just complain about it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading a crowd in front of the Muni stop on Larkin, harmonica in one hand, coffee in the other. Only in SF do bus delays turn into impromptu concerts.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the heart is really in the small plazas where locals sip vermut and gossip, not in the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the tram stops – overly scanning maps, yet somehow still missed the ‘bon dia’ from locals.
